clue.text: UK film co's revamped traditional notes

indicators.note: to revamp something is to rework it, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A British movie studio has reworked some old-fashioned memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' is the anagram signal, and 'notes' are musical ones rather than memos.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs and tunes handed down among ordinary people are traditional by nature, a whimsical description of the genre.

clue.text: Exclusive bail

definitions.meaning: a news story one paper gets ahead of its rivals
to bail is to ladle water out of a boat

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a journalist's story beaten out of rivals, and a verb for ladling water out of a boat.

clue.text: "King needs a wash", mother reflected in capital

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the run after the king is read backwards

parts.note: waves lap or wash against a shore
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother's remark that the monarch could do with a bath is mirrored in the chief city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' governs all three pieces after the king, read backwards as one run; the quotation marks are only dressing for the story.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the chief city of Uganda, an example of a seat of government.

clue.text: Scientist stopped by wide urban development

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the wide goes inside the scientist

parts.note: Isaac Newton, the physicist
W is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A researcher is held up by a sprawling building project in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped by' means plugged by, not halted by. In Britain these are planned settlements built from scratch after the war, such as Milton Keynes or Stevenage.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned settlement built from scratch is an example of city building.

clue.text: Puzzling symbols, etc, on vehicle

parts.note: re means on the subject of
a bus is a passenger vehicle

explanation.surface: Baffling signs and the like are painted on a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is not a position word here: it gives RE, as in 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture riddle in which drawings, letters and signs stand for a word or phrase.

clue.text: Most tiresome ducks crossing river close to boat

indicators.note: to cross is to go over or span, so the ducks go around the river

parts.note: ducks, like dearies, is a British term of endearment
R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the boat is taken

explanation.surface: The most annoying waterfowl paddle over a stream right next to a dinghy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' is a British endearment ('all right, ducks?'), not birds; 'crossing' wraps it round R and 'close to' takes the T of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: the dullest, most wearisome thing of all.

clue.text: Pine for knight despatched by coward

indicators.note: to despatch is to send away, so the coward sends off the knight

parts.note: a craven is an old word for a cowardly person
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A damsel longs for the champion sent off by a poltroon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despatched by' removes the N from CRAVEN; 'Pine for' looks like part of the story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to long for or yearn after something.

clue.text: Rising wind enthralling black cat

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so the wind holds the black inside

parts.note: to reel thread is to wind it
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A strengthening gale fascinates a dark moggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' is the verb, to coil; 'enthralling' puts B inside REEL. 'Rising' is a noun, an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for an uprising or revolt against authority.

clue.text: Biker uses this local name upfront

indicators.note: upfront says the name is placed ahead of the local

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
a local is British for a neighbourhood pub or bar

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist gives the nickname people know him by in the area before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upfront' is a placement word, not 'in advance'. A 'local' is what the British call their neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of bike equipment: the steering piece a rider grips.

clue.text: Bizarre course, heading back almost to finish

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, sent back to sit one place short of the end

parts.note: a route is a course to follow

explanation.surface: A weird racetrack doubles back just before the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading back almost to finish' shifts the R of ROUTE to next-to-last place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, borrowed from French: eccentric, beyond what is usual.

clue.text: No slimline actors on air?

parts.note: something not slim is wide or broad
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there are any thin performers on television at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical two-part reading: a company of players that is anything but slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: I mount docked horse for National

indicators.note: to dock a tail is to cut off the end, so the mount loses its last letter

parts.note: to mount is to rise or climb
H is slang for heroin, as horse is

explanation.surface: A jockey climbs onto a bob-tailed runner for the big steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the E from RISE. The surface evokes the Grand National, Britain's famous steeplechase, but 'National' just means a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a citizen of a particular country, here Ireland.

clue.text: Hands-on performance in playing piece

indicators.note: in places the performance inside the playing piece

parts.note: a tile is a piece in games such as mahjong or dominoes
an act is a turn or performance on stage

explanation.surface: A practical, involved rendition appears within a stage work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing piece' wants to be a stage play; it is a game token, and 'in' is the insertion signal, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning synonym: relating to the sense of touch.

clue.text: Wrap up warmly to haul back trailer

parts.note: to lag pipes is to wrap them in insulation

indicators.note: back says the hauling word is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: to drag is to haul along

explanation.surface: Put on a thick coat before towing the caravan home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAG into GARD. A 'trailer' is one who trails behind, not something towed.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning synonym: a straggler who trails behind the others.

clue.text: City left-winger backed Times

indicators.note: backed says the left-winger is written the other way round

parts.note: a red is a communist or socialist
times and by both express multiplication, as in two by four

explanation.surface: A footballer on the left flank gave his support to a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns RED into DER; 'Times' is the multiplication word, not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: On vacation, stay in shape jogging uphill

indicators.note: to jog something is to knock it out of position, so the letters are disturbed
to vacate is to empty, so the word stay loses its inside and keeps its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker keeps fit by running up slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties STAY to SY, and 'jogging' rearranges SY IN SHAPE. 'uphill' is the adjective, as in an uphill struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: Sisyphus forever pushed a boulder up a slope, so such a task is endlessly laborious.

clue.text: Mendicant's clean clothing stank ultimately

indicators.note: clothes go round a body, so the clean word wraps the letter

parts.note: a fair fight is a clean one

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of stank is taken

explanation.surface: A beggar's freshly washed garments ended up smelling awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' wraps FAIR round the K that 'ultimately' takes from stank.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Muslim or Hindu holy man who lives by begging.

clue.text: Idiot sheep, full of energy, drops

indicators.note: something full of another thing has it inside, so the sheep holds the energy

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep
E is the physics symbol for energy
rain falls as drops of water

explanation.surface: A daft ewe, bursting with vigour, falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts E inside LAMB; 'drops' is a noun, what falls from clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym for a stupid person.

clue.text: The average toff has good intentions

parts.note: the mean is the arithmetic average
toff and swell are both dated British slang for a posh, fashionable person

explanation.surface: Your typical upper-class gent wants to do the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff, like a swell, is dated British slang for a wealthy upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom said of someone whose aims are kind even if the results are not.

clue.text: Simpler to adopt English in guidelines for party leaders

indicators.note: in places the built word inside the guidelines

parts.note: standards are rules or guidelines to meet

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the simpler word takes in the letter

parts.note: a barer room is a plainer, simpler one

explanation.surface: It would be easier to use plain English in the rule book for those heading the political group.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'to adopt' builds the inner word and 'in' drops it into the guidelines, just before their final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: those who carry the flag at the front of a group or movement.

clue.text: Novel by Lear truncates early work

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters after it are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book by the nonsense poet Edward Lear cuts short something he wrote in his youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is the anagram signal, not a book; the work is Chaucer's fourteenth-century story collection, early in English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Chaucer's fourteenth-century collection of stories, among the first great books in English.

clue.text: Arable worker heard regularly chasing mother on farm

indicators.note: what chases comes behind, so the picked letters follow the farm mother

parts.note: a sow is a female pig, a mother in the farmyard

indicators.note: regularly takes letters at even intervals, here the second and fourth of heard

explanation.surface: A field hand can often be heard running after a parent across the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks from 'heard' alone, and 'chasing' is a position word; 'mother on farm' is one phrase for the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone who scatters seed on ploughed land.

clue.text: By sea, you could take in this old region

definitions.text: By sea, you could take in this

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old, as in OT
a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: Travelling by ship, you could see this ancient part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' means breathe in: seaside air was popularly called by this name and thought bracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular belief: the bracing seaside air people breathe was called this, after the gas.

clue.text: Remorse, with coppers bagging up European dosh

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a bag, so the coppers hold the other letters

parts.note: coppers are British low-value coins, pennies or pence

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: dosh and tin are both British slang for money

explanation.surface: Feeling guilty, a man watches police seize a pile of foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' are British small coins, not police. 'up' flips the European-plus-dosh pair to NITE before 'bagging' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sorrow and regret for a wrong done.

clue.text: School split by tradition came together under one roof

indicators.note: the school is cut in two with the tradition placed in the gap

parts.note: a coed is a co-educational school
a habit is a settled custom or tradition

explanation.surface: A college divided over an old custom was reunited in a single building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split by' is the insertion signal; 'School' is the adjective-turned-noun for one teaching boys and girls together.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: lived in the same home as a couple.

clue.text: How those lying see things improving?

definitions.meaning: people flat on their backs gaze towards the ceiling
said of a situation getting better

explanation.definitionFit: Literal picture of the gaze of someone flat on their back, and an idiom for a situation getting better.

clue.text: Varied recitation with no love involved

indicators.note: to vary is to change, so the letters are changed in order
with no says the letter for love is left out of the fodder

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A mixed programme of spoken verse leaves out anything romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops the O from recitation and 'Varied' rearranges the remaining nine letters. 'involved' is an adjective, complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complicated, with many interwoven parts.

clue.text: Commander standing, and heel's come off

indicators.note: in a down entry, something standing rises from the bottom, so the commander is written upwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
a heel, like a cur, is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A naval officer is on his feet and part of his shoe has fallen away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns CO upside down to OC; 'heel' is a cad, and 'come off' means take place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to happen or take place, as an event does.

clue.text: In age, one's making a bloomer

indicators.note: In places the letters for one's inside the age

parts.note: an age is an era or day, as in 'in this day'
one is I in Roman numerals, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: As you get older, you are prone to committing a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the insertion signal at the front. A 'bloomer' is British slang for a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flower, which blooms.

clue.text: I'm surprised academic was sporting

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: How unexpected that a professor turned out to be a good loser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' means wearing, not fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wore, as in sporting a hat.
